identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Padmanabhaswamy is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Vaishnavism, eulogised in the Tamil Divya Prabandham, where Nammalwar praises the temple and its city. The deity is worshipped in the Anantha Shayana form, reclining on the serpent Anantha, and is seen through three separate doors that reveal the head, the mid-section and the feet in turn. Since Marthanda Varma's Thrippadidanam of 1750 the rulers of Travancore have governed as Padmanabha Dasa, servants of the deity, which makes the temple the religious centre of the former kingdom as well as a pilgrimage site.

governance.establishedEra: Ancient origins; present structure 16th century · Built during the rule of Travancore rulers
governance.founderPatron: Extensively rebuilt and endowed by Marthanda Varma of Travancore, who dedicated the kingdom to the deity on 17 January 1750

narrative.summaryIntro:
Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Trivandrum, Kerala, is one of the most important temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is the presiding deity of the royal Travancore state. The temple is known for its significance in Vaishnavite tradition and its unique architectural blend of Dravidian and Kerala styles. The main sanctum features an impressive gopuram and ornate pillared corridors characteristic of Kerala temple architecture.

The temple gained international attention in 2011 when its underground vaults were opened, revealing treasures of immense historical and monetary value. The temple remains an important pilgrimage site for devotees of Vishnu and attracts thousands of visitors annually. The temple's architectural beauty, combined with its spiritual significance and rich heritage, makes it a major tourist and pilgrimage destination in Kerala. The temple complex exemplifies the artistic and religious traditions of South India.
narrative.documentedHistory:
The temple keeps an unusually deep documentary record. Around 1425 CE Veera Iravi Varma built a granta-pura, or record-room, to house temple documents, and more than 3,000 cadjan-leaf records were transferred to the Kerala Archives Department in 1867.

The temple as it now stands is largely the result of the reconstruction undertaken after Marthanda Varma's accession, completed in 906 Malayalam Era (1731 CE). On 17 January 1750 Marthanda Varma performed the Thrippadidanam, formally surrendering the Kingdom of Travancore to Padmanabhaswamy; the rulers thereafter styled themselves Padmanabha Dasa.

In 2011 five of the temple's underground vaults were opened under Supreme Court supervision, while the principal Vault B was left unopened. The litigation concluded with the judgment of 13 July 2020, which placed secular administration, assets and finances under a court-appointed Administrative Committee while leaving religious custom with the traditional bodies.

visitingInfo.entryRules: Only Hindus are permitted inside the temple.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Darshan slots are stated to vary during festivals and special occasions. Confirm the day's timings with the temple before travelling rather than relying on a published schedule.

openingHours.notes: Darshan slot as listed by Kerala Tourism; timings vary during festivals.

shrines.deityOrSubject: Vishnu as Padmanabha reclining on Anantha
shrines.locationDescription: The main sanctum, viewed through three separate doors: the first showing the head with the Shiva linga under the right hand, Sridevi and Brahma on the lotus; the second the abhisheka and utsava idols; the third the feet with Bhudevi and Markandeya Muni.
Holds an independent status within the complex, with its own namaskara mandapam, bali stones and flagmast.
A single granite slab about 20 feet square and 2.5 feet thick, brought from Tirumala village and installed in 1731; by custom only the ruler of Travancore prostrates upon it.
About 100 feet high, in Pandyan style, its foundation dated to 1566; an 80-foot flagstaff stands before the main entry.
Adjoins the temple on the east.

festivals.significance: One of the temple's two ten-day annual festivals, held in the Malayalam month of Meenam.
festivals.processionOrRituals: Concludes with the Aarat procession to Shankumugham Beach, the ruler of Travancore escorting the processional idols for the ritual sea bath.

festivals.significance: The second of the temple's two ten-day annual festivals, held in the Malayalam month of Thulam.
festivals.processionOrRituals: Also concludes with the Aarat procession to Shankumugham Beach.

festivals.significance: A sexennial observance in which a hundred thousand oil lamps are lit across the temple premises.
festivals.processionOrRituals: Preceded by fifty-six days of Murajapam, the chanting of the three Vedas.

festivals.significance: Idols of Saraswati Amman, Mun Uditha Nangai and Kumara Swami are brought in procession from Padmanabhapuram Palace, Suchindram and Kumarakovil for the nine days.
festivals.processionOrRituals: The Swathi Sangeethotsavam music festival is held in association with the observance.
